title: Node hibernation protocol and throughput safeguards for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) want lower unit costs by allowing nodes to enter a low-power hibernation state during predictable low-demand intervals (night/weekend), but any such optimization must preserve throughput guarantees and latency SLOs. Current maintenance/drain flows are designed for upgrades or hard decommissions and cause KV-cache warmup delays and capacity hiccups when hosts are removed and reintroduced.

Goal: Design and implement a controlled 'node hibernation' protocol that: (1) enables temporarily pausing a host (freeing compute for internal cost-saving or preemptible reuse) with fast reactivation, (2) preserves per-customer throughput reservations and SLOs by maintaining soft buffer lanes and prewarm strategies, and (3) integrates with autoscaler and fleet controls so the platform can reclaim or release hibernated capacity without causing customer-visible regressions.

Scope: This ticket covers the runtime protocol, autoscaler policy changes, KV-cache lifecycle management for hibernated nodes, console controls for schedule and manual hibernation, and rollout plan with canaries and load-tests. It does NOT include billing/pricing changes for hibernation discounts (handled by Finance/PM separate work).

Design overview:
- Hibernation state machine: Active -> DrainingSoft -> Hibernating -> Prewarming -> Active. DrainingSoft only allows non-new-session tokens and respects per-route throughput reservations; it does not evict in-flight KV sessions until a configurable grace window.
- Soft buffer lanes: Reserve configurable percent (default 15%) of fleet throughput as 'reserve lanes' that remain active when normal capacity drops; autoscaler must ensure reserve lanes remain satisfied when scheduling hibernation.
- KV-cache snapshot & fast-restore: On entering Hibernating, runtime persists compacted KV shards to S3-friendly blobstore (encrypted). Prewarm uses prioritized warmup of hottest keys for pinned customers. Snapshot size capped per-host to bound restore latencies.
- Autoscaler integration: Add hibernation-aware scaling policy that prefers hibernation before full host termination for short-term capacity balancing. Also a policy toggle to prefer immediate termination (for long-term scale-down).
- Console & API: Allow schedule rules (cron-like) per-dedicated-pool and per-host manual hibernate/unhibernate actions. Expose hibernation health metrics and predicted restore times.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Controlled hibernation can be scheduled for a dedicated pool with <1% increase in 95th latency across acceptance load tests compared to baseline.
2) Prewarm completes hot-KV restore for 80% of hottest keys within 30s in canary runs.
3) Autoscaler policy prevents hibernation if predicted demand within next 10 minutes would violate throughput reservations.
4) No data-plane errors (500s) attributable to hibernate/restore in 48h staging runs.
5) Console shows explicit hibernation state and estimated restore ETA; actions are auditable.

Milestones:
- Spike (2): prototype KV compact snapshot + restore flow, measure restore latency (by 2026-02-28)
- Runtime changes (5): implement state machine + soft drain behavior (by 2026-03-10)
- Autoscaler policy (3): add hibernation-aware scheduler and toggles (by 2026-03-18)
- Console/API (3): schedule UI and audit logs + RBAC gating (by 2026-03-22)
- Canary rollout (5): staged rollout to two dedicated pools, run chaos/load tests (by 2026-03-29)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Restore latency causes temporary SLO violations. Mitigation: conservative default reserve lanes + aggressive canary testing + circuit-breaker that aborts restore fallback to a warm standby model.
- Risk: Snapshot storage explosion. Mitigation: per-host compaction, TTLs, and deduplication in blobstore.
- Risk: Customer surprise due to invisible hibernation. Mitigation: explicit opt-out per-customer and transparency in Console and audit logs.

Rollout plan: Start with internal 'econ' dedicated pools (low criticality), 48h soak with synthetic load, then opt-in alpha customers for weekend-only hibernation. Monitor SLO, error budget burn, and KV restore metrics before broader rollout.

Telemetry to add: hibernate_enter, hibernate_exit, kv_snapshot_size_bytes, kv_restore_time_ms_p50/p95, reserve_lane_utilization, predicted_restore_eta_ms.
